title: Change request
description: The recorded request that originates every change to a governed repository. The named producer is whoever asked; the named consumers are every capability that needs to know what was asked and why it is being asked — impact analysis, root selection, the specification delta, and domain modelling all declare it. This contract existed as a deferral for as long as the method did: the specification that requires a change request for every change also defers its schema, and the deferral held until three capabilities declared the artifact without a contract version and so could not satisfy the rule that a prerequisite is declared with one. That is what this closes, and it is the whole of why it exists now rather than earlier. Its body stays prose on purpose. A request explains what someone wants, and where an artifact only explains something to a reader, prose is the correct form and a schema around it is ceremony. What the contract adds is identity, provenance, and the one field a predicate reads.

contract_version.description: The contract this instance declares. A consumer selects behaviour on this value and never infers a version from shape.

request_id.description: Stable identifier for this request. Six other contracts already carry a field of exactly this shape referring to it, which is what made the absence of this one visible: the identifier was validated everywhere except where the thing it identifies lives.

type.description: What kind of change is being asked for. The vocabulary is two values because exactly one predicate reads this field — a regulatory change escalates to the full path with a reinforced acceptance gate — and a third value would be a distinction nothing consumes. It widens when a predicate needs it to, and not before. `ordinary` is not a default the framework supplies: the requester states it, so that `regulatory` is a positive claim somebody made rather than the absence of one.

requested_by.description: Who asked. Provenance rather than authority: naming the requester does not make the request correct, and no capability reads this field to decide anything. It is here so a recorded decision can be traced to the ask that prompted it.

requested_at.description: When it was asked, as a UTC instant the caller supplies. The framework refuses to mint one, for the same reason it refuses elsewhere: an artifact stamped from a clock cannot be reproduced and compared.

statement.description: What is being asked, in prose. It states the problem or the outcome wanted, not how to build it — a request that specifies the solution has done the modelling that a later capability is accountable for, and done it where nothing records whether the request stated it or somebody decided it.

constraints.description: A constraint the request imposes that is not part of what it asks for — a deadline, a compatibility promise, a system that must keep working. Recorded separately from `statement` because a constraint binds the solution while the statement describes the problem, and a downstream capability treating one as the other either over-constrains the design or ignores a limit somebody stated.

out_of_scope.description: What the requester says this request does not cover. Optional here and required of a knowledge object, and the difference is deliberate: a knowledge object's silence would be read as permission by whatever generates from it, while a request's silence is answered by the analysis recording an open question. Where the requester does bound the ask, recording it saves the modelling step from asking.

artifacts.description: Each artifact this request was read from, by path or stable reference. Non-empty: a request nobody can re-read is a request nobody can check an analysis against, and every capability downstream carries this provenance forward into what it produces.
